_rules: Entries may NEVER be edited or removed. The only permitted change is status: 'failing' -> 'passing', and only after the criteria were verified against the running application.

features.feature: Mount reachability probe detects what existence checks miss
criteria: A configured additional_mount whose host path does not exist is reported as failing

A configured additional_mount whose host path EXISTS and is readable but which docker refuses with exit 125 is reported as failing — this is the case fs.realpathSync passes and is the whole reason the check exists
The report names the host-path-exists contradiction explicitly, so the reader does not start by ls-ing a directory that is demonstrably fine
Distinct host paths are deduped — two groups sharing one mount produce one probe, not two
A probe that hangs is killed by a timeout and reported as inconclusive, never wedging the caller
A non-125 non-zero exit is reported as a distinct category from a 125, because it means the image or entrypoint is wrong rather than the mount

features.feature: Escalation fires on state transition, not on every failure
criteria: healthy -> failing -> healthy produces exactly two admin DMs, not one per check run
A check that stays failing across many consecutive runs produces no further DMs after the first
Recovery produces a DM saying it recovered
Transition state survives a host restart — a restart during a failing period does not re-fire the alert
With every check healthy the runner produces no output and sends no DM

features.feature: Spawn failures back off instead of retrying identically forever
criteria: A spawn returning exit 125 records a failure against the agent group rather than only logging it
Repeated 125s back off rather than retrying every 60s sweep — the 2026-08-12 outage produced 2193 identical attempts in 13 hours
A successful spawn clears the backoff state for that group
Backoff never permanently disables a group — it caps at an interval and keeps retrying at that interval

features.feature: Doctor is invocable on demand and usable from cron
criteria: The command runs every registered check and prints one report
It exits non-zero when any check fails and zero when all pass, so cron and CI can use the exit code
It prints nothing alarming when everything is healthy
It is rejected for container (agent) callers — probing spawns containers on the host, so it is operator-only
Output is renderable as both human text and --json
A messaging_groups row whose channel_type has no registered adapter is reported, naming the group and the channel
A messaging_groups row with zero messaging_group_agents rows is reported as unwired
Rows deliberately left unwired are suppressible so known-good exceptions like Signal Note-to-Self stay quiet
A fully wired install with all adapters present produces no output at all

features.feature: A scheduled task series that stops running is reported (2026-08-11 -> 08-15 miss)
criteria: A task series with 2 or more consecutive failed runs is reported as failing, well before the scheduler's own auto-pause cap of 8
A series already auto-paused is reported as failing and the report carries the exact `ncl tasks resume <id>` command
A single failed run does not alert — one miss is usually transient
The result id is the series id, so escalation tracks the same subject across runs and alerts once, not nightly
A healthy armed series produces no output
Verified against the live install: trip-planner-build-722c (paused, 8 fails) and trip-planner-watch-6049 (4 fails) are both caught, dm-with-smergler's two hourly series both pass
